title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 69-72). Grothendieck works with half-simplicial (semi-simplicial, no degeneracies) objects with values in an additive tensor category B, written B^·. He has categories of 'universal models' (P^2_*, B^·_*, P_{0*}, K_*), built from the standard semi-simplicial cochain objects C^·_* (with Ψ^0_* = Z^0_* the constant/unit object), and a bi-indexed version (**) for exterior products. A complex C^· in B^· with a 'multiplicative structure' is encoded by a tensor-compatible functor F = F_{C^·} from the model category to B with F(C^·_*) = C^·. The previous page proved that such a structure is uniquely determined, using Σ-resolutions, injectivity of the comparison map (Dold-Puppe formulas) and an analysis of the unit axiom.

This page states a transfer principle. Any 'universal' construction in the model categories that uses only (i) the notion of h-linear/h-injective (homotopy-injective) structure and (ii) the tensor structures is reflected in an analogous construction on every multiplicative C^· in B^·.

Example 1 (cup product). The external product C^·_* ⊛ C^·_* is a Σ-projective resolution of the unit Z^0_{**} in the bi-indexed category P_{0**}. C^·_* is h-injective, so comparison of resolutions gives a map Tot^·(C^·_* ⊛ C^·_*) → C^·_*. This map is unique up to homotopy, which is an acyclic-models/Eilenberg-Zilber-type argument. Applying F_{C^·} gives F_C(C_* ⊛ C_*) → F(C_*) = C^·. Precomposing with the structure map C ⊗_B C = F_C(C) ⊗_B F_C(C) → F_C(C_* ⊛ C_*) yields a product C^· ⊗_B C^· → C^·, defined up to homotopy. By the same uniqueness argument it is associative, graded-commutative ('attention aux signes!') and unital up to homotopy. So C^· becomes a homotopy-commutative '⊗_B-algebra', i.e. a commutative monoid in the homotopy category.

The page closes with an open question: does H^*(C^·) then have the usual properties (graded-commutative ring, functoriality, etc.)?

Purpose: to equip the cohomology of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes (dévissage setting) with cup products intrinsically, from a multiplicative structure on the universal models. The next page applies the same principle to a divided-power de Rham complex as a strictly commutative bigraded model.
errors: No mathematical error is visible, but the structure obtained is only up to homotopy (a commutative monoid in the homotopy category), not coherent. Higher homotopies (A∞/E∞ data) are not addressed.
The signs needed for graded commutativity are flagged but not checked.
The claim that C_* ⊛ C_* is a Σ-projective resolution of Z^0_{**} rests on Dold-Puppe/Eilenberg-Zilber-type facts from the previous pages; it is not reproved here.

ideas.what: Transfer principle: universal constructions on standard models, using only homotopy-injectivity and tensor structure, induce constructions on any complex with a multiplicative structure (encoded as a tensor functor out of the model category).
ideas.modern_name: Method of acyclic models / universal example; prefigures operadic 'action of the endomorphisms of the universal object'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg-MacLane (acyclic models, 1953); operadic formulation by May, Boardman-Vogt (1970s)
ideas.where_published: Related 'modelizer' philosophy in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs, but not this specific formulation

ideas.what: Product Tot(C_* ⊛ C_*) → C_* obtained by comparison of resolutions, unique up to homotopy, giving a homotopy-associative, commutative and unital cup product C ⊗_B C → C.
ideas.modern_name: Cup product via Eilenberg-Zilber / Alexander-Whitney; homotopy-commutative algebra structure on cochains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg-Zilber, Alexander-Whitney, Godement (Topologie algébrique et théorie des faisceaux)
ideas.where_published: Analogous cup-product constructions appear in SGA 4 / SGA 4½ (cohomology with products), not in this form

ideas.what: Question of whether H^*(C^·) inherits the usual properties of a cohomology ring.

missed.claim: Encoding a 'multiplicative structure' on a semi-simplicial complex as a tensor functor F_C from a category of universal models is close to later operadic and Lawvere-theory treatments of cochain algebras. In those treatments, all natural operations come from the universal object. Grothendieck stops at homotopy level, but the framework would naturally carry the coherent E∞ structure.
missed.quote: Toutes les constructions ("universelles") dans P^2_* ... qui ne font intervenir que la notion de structure h-lin. et les ⊗-structures, se reflètent dans constructions analogues sur une C^· ∈ B^· munie de structure multiplicative.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mild historical anticipation (c. 1975-76) of the model-theoretic approach to E∞ cochains, as in Mandell, McClure-Smith and Hinich-Schechtman. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard acyclic-models derivation of a homotopy-commutative cup product in Grothendieck's own semi-simplicial/tensor framework. The general 'universal models transfer' phrasing is slightly forward-looking (operadic flavour), but the result itself is classical.
transcription_corrections: 'notion de structure h-libre' is more likely 'structure h-lin.' (h-linear/h-injective).
The structure map line reads 'F_{C^·}(C^·) ⊗_B F_{C^·}(C^·)' (subscript C on both factors), not 'F_{C^·}(C^·) ⊗_B F(C^·)'.
In 'comme C^·_* ⊗ C^·_* est une résolution', the product is the external product ⊛ (C^·_* ⊛ C^·_*), matching Tot^·(C^·_* ⊛ C^·_*).
The note under Tot (arrow downward) is illegible; 'contractible' is uncertain.
The struck-out passage after 'Ex!' contains 'C^·_* ⊛ C^·_*' and 'Θ', not 'H^·(C^*_*)'.
